scope: Properties only. No model, cfg, code, test or TLC execution in this call. Evidence is limited to old/source, new/source, update.patch and old/spec.
overall_reason: Keep the reference safety/structural/liveness suite (no guarantee there is weakened by this update). Revise four properties whose guarantee changed in the source: AutoLeaveAdvance (auto-leave now fires on a crossing of pendingConfIndex, cannot be refused, and bumps pendingConfIndex), OutcomeSoundness and ProposalConfigurationDecisions (leader refuses conf changes based on whether the config is joint; zero-size entries are exempt from the quota), and ConfigurationTransitionSafety (its id=0 exclusion also hid leader-generated leave-joint entries). Add properties for behavior that no existing property observes: auto-leave really happens, pendingConfIndex covers every unapplied conf entry, applied conf changes are classified correctly against joint/non-joint config, a demoted transferee aborts the transfer, and newly added replicas are probed immediately. Add canaries so focused checking actually reaches the changed paths. Three implementation-defect candidates (D1-D3) must not be hidden by these edits. They are visible only through the new properties AutoLeaveInitiated and ConfChangeApplyClassification and the retained NoUnexpectedFatal, not through properties that restate the new guards.

update_summary.change: advance(): auto-leave now fires only when applied crosses pendingConfIndex (oldApplied < pendingConfIndex <= newApplied). It uses nil Data (payload 0), panics if the entry is refused, always sets pendingConfIndex = lastIndex after appending, and reduceUncommittedSize now runs first.
evidence: testdata/confchange_v2_add_double_auto.txt:238-279 (regression comment: duplicate leave used to panic)

update_summary.change: stepLeader MsgProp: each conf entry (V1/V2) is refused (rewritten to an empty EntryNormal) if alreadyPending, or if joint && !wantsLeaveJoint, or if !joint && wantsLeaveJoint. wantsLeaveJoint is len(AsV2().Changes)==0. Unmarshal errors panic.
increaseUncommittedSize: a zero-size batch is never refused (adds the s>0 condition).

confchange initProgress: Next = LastIndex (was LastIndex+1). switchToConfig at a leader: if maybeCommit is false, it now runs maybeSendAppend(id, sendIfEmpty=false) for every progress, so new replicas are probed immediately with the last entry.

switchToConfig: a leader transfer is aborted if the transferee is no longer in Voters.IDs() (both joint halves). Before, it was aborted only if the transferee had no Progress, so a demotion did not abort it.

confchange.Simple: removed a redundant checkInvariants early return that returned an empty config with a nil error. Invariant failures now surface as errors from checkAndReturn (applyConfChange panics).

Same behavior, different code: campaign sorts vote recipients; unstable.maybeTerm refactor; IsEmptyHardState; lease-read ri; ConfChangeV2 methods now use value receivers; restore comment typo. Test-only: rafttest InteractionEnv and datadriven testdata.

Side effect of C4 on raft.restore: confchange.Restore builds progress with Next=lastIndex, and pr.MaybeUpdate(pr.Next-1) now leaves the follower's self Match at snapshotIndex-1. Follower-only, and reset on campaign.

entries.name: AutoLeaveAdvance
evidence: testdata/confchange_v2_add_double_auto.txt:238-279 (old level-triggered behavior appended duplicate leaves, causing a panic)
raft_test.go:251-258 (an empty entry is always appendable)
entries.observer: Replace autoLeaveChecks.eligible (a guard computed inside the observer) with raw fields: [autoLeave |-> r.config.autoLeave, role |-> r.role, appliedBefore |-> r.applied, cursor |-> b.cursor, pendingBefore |-> r.pendingConf, pendingAfter |-> a.pendingConf, beforeLast |-> Last(r), beforeHist |-> Hist(r), afterHist |-> Hist(a), fatalAfter |-> a.fatal]
entries.expression:
AutoLeaveAdvance_new == \A a \in history.autoLeaveChecks:
  LET trig == a.autoLeave /\ a.role="Leader" /\ a.cursor>0 /\ a.appliedBefore<a.pendingBefore /\ a.cursor>=a.pendingBefore
      e == a.afterHist[Len(a.afterHist)]
  IN IF trig THEN /\ a.fatalAfter=""
                  /\ Len(a.afterHist)=a.beforeLast+1 /\ Prefix(a.afterHist,a.beforeLast)=a.beforeHist
                  /\ IsLeave(e) /\ e.id=0 /\ e.weight=0
                  /\ a.pendingAfter=Len(a.afterHist)
     ELSE a.afterHist=a.beforeHist /\ a.pendingAfter=a.pendingBefore
entries.rationale: The source guarantee changed. The trigger is now a crossing, not a level. The DropQuota retry branch is gone because the entry cannot be refused (a refusal panics). pendingConfIndex must equal the leave index. The old property demands an append on every level-eligible Advance, which the fixed source rightly does not do. This property restates the source guard, so it cannot detect a missed trigger. AutoLeaveInitiated is added for that (see D1/D3). Remove the old AutoLeaveAdvance from cfg enablement (it is enabled only through UpdateAutoLeaveAdvance in Update_full/Update_focused).

entries.name: OutcomeSoundness
entries.observer: Extend the outcome record with entries |-> m.entries, joint |-> raft[n].config.outgoing#{}, pending |-> raft[n].pendingConf, applied |-> raft[n].applied. The property no longer reads the model-computed weight from RewriteConf.
entries.expression:
WantsLeave(e) == e.kind="V2" /\ e.changes=<<>>
RECURSIVE AdmittedConf(_,_)
AdmittedConf(o,K) == IF K=0 THEN {} ELSE
  LET prev==AdmittedConf(o,K-1) e==o.entries[K]
      refuse==(o.pending>o.applied \/ prev#{}) \/ (o.joint /\ ~WantsLeave(e)) \/ (~o.joint /\ WantsLeave(e))
  IN IF e.kind \in ConfKinds /\ ~refuse THEN prev \cup {K} ELSE prev
Effective(o) == [k \in DOMAIN o.entries |-> IF o.entries[k].kind \in ConfKinds /\ k \notin AdmittedConf(o,Len(o.entries)) THEN Entry(0,0,"Normal",0,0,0,EmptyEncoded) ELSE o.entries[k]]
ExpectedDecision_new(o) == IF o.role="Leader" THEN
    IF ~o.member THEN "DropRemoved" ELSE IF o.transfer#0 THEN "DropTransfer"
    ELSE IF o.quota>0 /\ Weight(Effective(o))>0 /\ o.quota+Weight(Effective(o))>MaxUncommitted THEN "DropQuota" ELSE "Accepted"
  ELSE IF o.role#"Follower" \/ o.lead=0 THEN "DropNoLeader"
  ELSE IF ~o.forwarding THEN "DropForwardDisabled" ELSE "Forwarded"
OutcomeSoundness_new == \A o \in history.outcomes: o.decision=ExpectedDecision_new(o)
entries.rationale: Two changed guarantees: zero-size batches are never dropped by the quota (s>0), and conf entries are rewritten by the joint-state admission rule. The weight is now computed inside the property, so the property no longer depends on the draft's RewriteConf. Replace OutcomeSoundness with OutcomeSoundness_new wherever it is enabled (hunt_3*, hunt_6, Trace, TraceCorrespondence).

entries.observer: ProposalObservation adds joint |-> r.config.outgoing#{} and pendingAfter |-> a.pendingConf.
entries.expression:
ProposalContract_new(o) ==
  LET adm==AdmittedConf(o,Len(o.entries)) eff==Effective(o) w==Weight(eff)
      expected==IF o.role="Leader" THEN
          IF o.node \notin o.voters \cup o.learners THEN "DropRemoved"
          ELSE IF o.transfer#0 THEN "DropTransfer"
          ELSE IF o.quota>0 /\ w>0 /\ o.quota+w>MaxUncommitted THEN "DropQuota" ELSE "Accepted"
        ELSE IF o.role#"Follower" \/ o.lead=0 THEN "DropNoLeader"
        ELSE IF o.noForward THEN "DropForwardDisabled" ELSE "Forwarded"
  IN /\ o.decision=expected
     /\ IF expected="Accepted" THEN [old content clauses of ProposalContract with effective := eff] ELSE o.after=o.before
     /\ (o.role="Leader" /\ expected \in {"Accepted","DropQuota"} =>
           o.pendingAfter = IF adm={} THEN o.pending ELSE Len(o.before)+MaxSet(adm))
ProposalConfigurationDecisions_new == \A o \in quality.proposals: ProposalContract_new(o)
entries.rationale: Pins the source's admission semantics: wantsLeave = V2 with no changes (len(Changes)==0), regardless of Transition, evaluated against the leader's current joint state. pendingConfIndex is bumped per admitted entry before appendEntry (raft.go:1070,1075), so it is bumped even on DropQuota. If the model admitted via IsLeave instead of WantsLeave, this property would flag the difference, so D2 cannot be hidden. Replace the old property in every cfg that enables it.

entries.name: AutoLeaveInitiated
entries.category: new safety (contract proxy for an auto-leave obligation)
evidence: raftpb/raft.proto:111-113 (auto_leave: 'Raft will automatically transition into the final config ... when this is safe')
entries.expression:
AutoLeaveInitiated == \A n \in Server: LET r==raft[n] IN
  ( /\ r.alive /\ r.fatal="" /\ r.role="Leader" /\ r.config.autoLeave
    /\ r.applied>0 /\ Term(r,r.applied)=r.term
    /\ Len(application[n].hist)>=r.applied )
  => \E k \in (r.applied+1)..Last(r): IsLeave(Hist(r)[k])
entries.rationale: This states the contract independently of the guard formula. A leader that has applied an entry of its own term, whose application has caught up with raft's applied index, and that is still in an autoLeave joint config must already have a leave-joint entry pending. It exposes D1 (leader elected with applied == lastIndex never crosses pendingConfIndex) and D3a (EarlyAdvance before ApplyConfChange). It also guards against a model that copies the source's trigger. Enable it in Update_full, Update_focused, Update_hunt_joint (EarlyAdvance=FALSE isolates D1 from D3) and TraceCorrespondence.

entries.name: PendingConfCoverage
evidence: new/source/raft.go:581 (auto-leave bump; absent in old: update.patch:647-653)
entries.expression:
PendingConfCoverage == \A n \in Server: LET r==raft[n] IN
  (r.alive /\ r.fatal="" /\ r.role="Leader") =>
    \A k \in (r.applied+1)..Last(r): Hist(r)[k].kind \in ConfKinds => k <= r.pendingConf
entries.rationale: The joint-state admission check is sound only if pendingConfIndex covers every unapplied conf entry in the leader's log. The old source violated this after a successful auto-leave append, which was the root cause of duplicate leaves. If a draft drops the pendingConf bump, this property catches it.

entries.name: ConfChangeApplyClassification
entries.category: interaction (admission observed through the old ApplyEntry consumer)
evidence: new/source/raft.go:1497-1517 (LeaveJoint vs EnterJoint vs Simple dispatch; panic on error)
raftpb/raft.proto:164-168 ('Leaving the joint configuration is accomplished by proposing a ConfChangeV2 with only and optionally the Context field populated')
entries.expression:
ConfChangeApplyClassification == \A o \in quality.effects:
  o.entry.kind \in ConfKinds => (IsLeave(o.entry) <=> o.before.outgoing # {})
entries.rationale: The new admission rules and the auto-leave deduplication exist so that every committed conf change applies without a changer error: a leave only on a joint config, and anything else only on a non-joint config. The check runs at the old consumer, so it catches D2 ({[], JointImplicit|JointExplicit} admitted in a joint config, then EnterJoint panics), D3b/D3c (stale-config decisions under EarlyAdvance) and any duplicate leave. Canceled V1 entries are deliberately included: the source still calls Simple, which errors in a joint config.

entries.name: LeaderTransferAbort
entries.observer: EffectObservation adds role |-> r.role, fatalAfter |-> a.fatal, selfPromotableAfter |-> (r.id \in VoterIDs(a.config) /\ r.id \notin a.config.learners), transferBefore |-> r.transfer, transferAfter |-> a.transfer, membersBefore |-> Members(r), membersAfter |-> Members(a).
entries.rationale: Checks both directions. The transfer is aborted when the transferee leaves both voter halves, whether removed or demoted after leave-joint. It is kept while the transferee sits in LearnersNext (still an outgoing voter), and it is untouched when switchToConfig returns early (leader removed or demoted). The old model's Members-based abort would fail this property.

entries.name: NewReplicaProbe
evidence: new/source/raft.go:453-457 (empty batch with sendIfEmpty=false returns before the snapshot fallback)
entries.observer: EffectObservation adds firstBefore |-> First(r), lastBefore |-> Last(r), outBefore |-> r.out, outAfter |-> a.out (plus the LeaderTransferAbort fields).
entries.expression:
NewReplicaProbe == \A o \in quality.effects: LeaderApplies(o) =>
  \A p \in (o.membersAfter \ o.membersBefore) \ {o.node}: o.lastBefore >= o.firstBefore =>
    \E m \in DOMAIN o.outAfter: /\ m.type="MsgApp" /\ m.from=o.node /\ m.to=p
      /\ m.index=o.lastBefore-1 /\ m.entries#<<>> /\ m.entries[1].index=o.lastBefore
      /\ o.outAfter[m] > (IF m \in DOMAIN o.outBefore THEN o.outBefore[m] ELSE 0)
entries.rationale: Ties the two coupled changes together. A replica gets a probe at Last-1 carrying the last entry in the same step, whichever maybeCommit branch is taken. A draft that changes only Next or only the probe fails this: with Next=Last+1 the sendIfEmpty=false probe sends nothing. The fully-compacted case (Last<First) is excluded because the source sends nothing there on the non-commit branch.

entries.name: AutoLeaveProgress
entries.category: new liveness (not enabled in bounded MC)
entries.expression:
AutoLeaveProgress == \A n \in Server:
  (StableLeader(n) /\ StableServices /\ FairCaller /\ FairNetwork /\ WF_vars(\E t \in Timeouts: Tick(n,t)))
    => (raft[n].config.autoLeave ~> ~raft[n].config.autoLeave)
entries.rationale: Temporal form of the auto_leave contract. Like the existing progress properties it needs an unbounded driver and stays commented out in the bounded cfgs. AutoLeaveInitiated is its checkable safety proxy.

entries.name: JointConfRefusalNotReached
entries.expression: JointConfRefusalNotReached == ~\E o \in quality.proposals: o.role="Leader" /\ o.joint /\ o.pending<=o.applied /\ \E k \in DOMAIN o.entries: o.entries[k].kind \in ConfKinds /\ ~WantsLeave(o.entries[k])
entries.rationale: Shows that the 'must transition out of joint config first' refusal is exercised.

entries.name: EmptyConfRefusalNotReached
entries.expression: EmptyConfRefusalNotReached == ~\E o \in quality.proposals: o.role="Leader" /\ ~o.joint /\ o.pending<=o.applied /\ \E k \in DOMAIN o.entries: WantsLeave(o.entries[k])
entries.rationale: Shows that the 'not in joint state; refusing empty conf change' refusal is exercised.

entries.name: NonAutoEmptyV2InJointNotReached
entries.expression: NonAutoEmptyV2InJointNotReached == ~\E o \in quality.proposals: o.role="Leader" /\ o.joint /\ o.pending<=o.applied /\ \E k \in DOMAIN o.entries: o.entries[k].kind="V2" /\ o.entries[k].changes=<<>> /\ o.entries[k].transition#"Auto"
entries.rationale: Shows that D2's trigger is reachable. If it is never reached, a passing ConfChangeApplyClassification is vacuous for D2.

entries.name: DemotedTransfereeAbortNotReached
entries.expression: DemotedTransfereeAbortNotReached == ~\E o \in quality.effects: o.transferBefore#0 /\ o.transferBefore \in o.membersAfter /\ o.transferBefore \notin VoterIDs(o.after) /\ o.transferAfter=0

entries.name: NewReplicaProbeNotReached

suspected_defects.summary: The crossing-based auto-leave misses a leader elected while its config is autoLeave-joint and its applied index equals lastIndex at election. becomeLeader sets pendingConfIndex=lastIndex, so oldApplied < pendingConfIndex never holds, no leave is appended, and the joint config stays until the application proposes one manually. The old level-triggered code handled this case (while duplicating leaves).
reachability_aid: Update_hunt_joint-style cfg with EarlyAdvance=FALSE, Tick/Campaign budget, optional crash
suspected_defects.must_not_hide_by: Do not narrow AutoLeaveInitiated to the source trigger condition, and do not drop it because AutoLeaveAdvance_new passes.

suspected_defects.summary: Admission and apply disagree on what a leave is. stepLeader treats any ConfChangeV2 with no Changes as a leave (len==0), but LeaveJoint() also requires Transition==Auto. {Changes:[], Transition:JointImplicit|JointExplicit} is therefore admitted in a joint config and then EnterJoint fails with 'config is already joint', and applyConfChange panics. In a non-joint config the same proposal is refused, although applying it would be a valid no-change joint entry.
suspected_defects.must_not_hide_by: Model admission must use WantsLeave (changes=<<>>), not IsLeave; ProposalConfigurationDecisions_new enforces this. Do not exclude non-Auto empty V2 batches from V2Batches.

suspected_defects.summary: Stale config under early Advance. README:122 allows Advance any time after persistence, i.e. before ApplyConfChange. advance() reads r.prs.Config.AutoLeave and stepLeader reads r.prs.Config joint state, but both use raftLog.applied for indices, so they can act on a stale config. (a) The auto-leave trigger can be missed permanently. (b) A duplicate leave can be appended while an earlier leave is applied but not yet ApplyConfChange'd. (c) A non-leave can be admitted against a stale non-joint config. (b) and (c) end in panics.

suspected_defects.summary: CampaignContract counts committed-unapplied V2 entries as pending, but StepHup/numOfPendingConf counts only EntryConfChange (V1). The V2-centric V03 focus and auto-leave entries make a campaign with a pending V2 entry reachable.
suspected_defects.must_not_hide_by: Do not change CampaignContract to LegacyConfKinds without validation evidence.

suspected_defects.summary: AdvanceCore keeps the DropQuota retry and AutoLeaveWeight=2/10, and triggers on the level cursor>=pendingConf. It must use weight 0, the oldApplied crossing, pendingConf=Last after the append, and Fatal on refusal. AppendQuotaExceeded needs Weight(es)>0. Otherwise AutoLeaveAdvance_new and OutcomeSoundness_new fail for model reasons.

ChangeProgress still creates Progress(0,last+1,TRUE). ApplyConfCore lacks the non-commit probe over all Members (sendEmpty=FALSE) and aborts the transfer on Members instead of VoterIDs. Restore self progress should be (s.index-1, s.index).

unresolved_obligations: Validation must classify any violations of AutoLeaveInitiated, ConfChangeApplyClassification and NoUnexpectedFatal against D1, D2 and D3 as model, property or implementation issues. No property edit may close them.

Decide whether Advance before ApplyConfChange (EarlyAdvance=TRUE) is a legal caller schedule (README.md:122 suggests yes). Run AutoLeaveInitiated under both EarlyAdvance=FALSE (isolates D1/D2) and TRUE (adds D3).

Observer extensions are required before checking: ProposalObservation (+joint, +pendingAfter), outcome record (+entries, +joint, +pending, +applied), autoLeaveChecks (raw fields in place of eligible), EffectObservation (+role, fatalAfter, selfPromotableAfter, transferBefore/After, membersBefore/After, firstBefore, lastBefore, outBefore/outAfter).
Re-measure the encoded size of the nil-Data auto-leave entry for Trace (AutoLeaveEncoded). The payload weight must be 0 (util.go:160-162).

Regenerate traces from new/source. The new testdata/*.txt interaction scenarios (confchange_v1_*, confchange_v2_*, snapshot_succeed_via_app_resp) are good trace candidates for AutoLeaveAdvance_new, NewReplicaProbe and ProposalConfigurationDecisions_new.

Cfg reachability. Update_focused has TransferLimit=0 (no LeaderTransferAbort coverage), all Update cfgs have Joining={} (NewReplicaProbe needs a remove then re-add or a Joining server), and Update_full has PayloadWeights={0,1} with MaxUncommitted=3 (cannot exercise the C3 quota bypass). Each new canary needs a dedicated hunt cfg.
AutoLeaveProgress and the other liveness properties remain unchecked until an unbounded service driver exists (MC.tla:82-87).
D4 (V1-only pending check at Hup) predates this patch. Enable CampaignDecisionEligibility in a separate V2 hunt cfg so that its expected candidate violation does not mask the V03 checks.

Low priority: when maybeCommit is false, the new switchToConfig Visit also probes self. This is harmless while self Next=Last+1 (re-adding self while leader is unreachable through the public API), but a draft that recreates self progress would emit a self-addressed MsgApp.
